title: MTU Mismatch Detection
exclusions: The primary detection compares the link MTU reported by `ip -j -d link show` with an explicitly approved value for the same exact `(host, interface)` in `linux_mtu_policy.csv`. It does not infer an intended MTU from other interfaces, treat mixed MTUs on one host as an error, inspect a switch or hypervisor, discover an end-to-end path MTU, prove packet loss or application impact, identify the constraining hop, validate TCP MSS, change network configuration, or cover interfaces absent from the policy. Optional ICMP Echo probes are retained as separate path-MTU evidence; a large-probe failure can also result from ICMP filtering, rate limiting, ECMP, congestion, endpoint policy, or a stale kernel route cache and is not relabeled as a configuration mismatch. The collector sees only the network namespace in which it runs. This operational UC provides no security detection or regulatory attestation.
evidence: After deployment, retain the versioned `linux_mtu_configuration_mismatch` saved-search definition and schedule, the effective `TA_linux_mtu` scripted-input and JSON extraction configuration, collector hash, a versioned export and approval record for `linux_mtu_policy.csv`, source-freshness results, alert dispatch rows, and the adjacent raw `event_kind=link` event for each finding. Keep optional `linux_mtu_path_probe_evidence` results, exact probe configuration, raw diagnostic text, route/path observations, and incident linkage in a separate evidence set so path behavior is never presented as proof of local configuration drift. Preserve dated positive and negative control-test output. These artifacts show what the collector, lookup, and search observed; this documentation-only review created no runtime evidence and did not validate production behavior.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, ingest one fresh JSON link event with `host=mtu-test`, `source=linux_mtu_snapshot`, `sourcetype=linux:mtu`, `event_kind=link`, `interface=eth0`, `link_mtu=1500`, and a numeric `collection_epoch`. Provide exactly one enabled lookup row for `(mtu-test,eth0)` with `expected_link_mtu=9000`, `policy_id=LAB-JUMBO-01`, and owner/role values. Run the primary SPL with only the index changed to the test index. Expect exactly one row with `signal_type=configuration_mismatch`, `observed_link_mtu=1500`, `expected_link_mtu=9000`, and `delta_bytes=-7500`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run four isolated cases and require zero primary-search rows: (1) `eth0=1500` with policy 1500; (2) one host with `eth0=1500` and `bond0=9000`, with each exact interface matching its own enabled policy; (3) a fresh `event_kind=path_probe` event where a small probe succeeds and the target-sized probe fails, but all link events match policy; and (4) a link event with no policy row. Case 2 proves heterogeneous interface MTUs are not inherently mismatches, case 3 proves path evidence is not promoted to local configuration drift, and case 4 remains a separately monitored policy-coverage defect rather than an assumed mismatch.

dataSources: Compact JSON events in the locally defined `index=os sourcetype=linux:mtu source=linux_mtu_snapshot`. A deployment-owned Universal Forwarder scripted input executes `ip -j -d link show` every five minutes and emits one `event_kind=link` event per interface with `interface`, `ifindex`, `link_mtu`, `operstate`, `link_type`, `master`, and `collection_epoch`. The primary SPL enriches the latest event from the exact-match `linux_mtu_policy.csv` lookup (`host`, `interface`, `expected_link_mtu`, `policy_id`, `interface_role`, `policy_owner`, `policy_enabled`). An optional 15-minute mode emits `event_kind=path_probe` results from controlled `ping -4/-6 -M do` tests, including small/target payload outcomes and any reported next-hop MTU. All names are deployment conventions, not fields supplied by Splunk or `Splunk_TA_nix`.
app: Deployment-owned `TA_linux_mtu` app containing the Universal Forwarder scripted input, collector, JSON source-type configuration, lookup, saved searches, and dashboard objects. It uses host-provided Python 3, iproute2 `ip`, and optional iputils `ping`; no Splunkbase or premium app is required. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) may coexist for other host telemetry but does not document this event or policy contract and is not the collector for this UC.
spl:
index=os sourcetype=linux:mtu source=linux_mtu_snapshot event_kind=link host=* earliest=-30m
| eval link_mtu=tonumber(link_mtu), collection_epoch=tonumber(collection_epoch)
| where isnotnull(interface) AND isnotnull(link_mtu) AND link_mtu>0 AND isnotnull(collection_epoch)
| sort 0 - _time
| dedup host interface
| rename _time as observed_time link_mtu as observed_link_mtu
| lookup linux_mtu_policy.csv host interface OUTPUT expected_link_mtu policy_id interface_role policy_owner policy_enabled
| eval expected_link_mtu=tonumber(expected_link_mtu), policy_enabled=lower(coalesce(policy_enabled,"false"))
| where policy_enabled="true" AND isnotnull(expected_link_mtu) AND expected_link_mtu>0 AND observed_link_mtu!=expected_link_mtu
| eval signal_type="configuration_mismatch", delta_bytes=observed_link_mtu-expected_link_mtu, age_seconds=now()-observed_time
| where age_seconds>=0 AND age_seconds<=1200
| sort 0 host interface
| table observed_time host interface interface_role operstate link_type master observed_link_mtu expected_link_mtu delta_bytes policy_id policy_owner collection_epoch age_seconds signal_type
description: Finds fresh Linux interface configurations whose observed link MTU differs from the approved MTU for that exact host and interface. It uses `ip` JSON snapshots and an owned policy lookup; it does not infer that interfaces on one host should share a value. Controlled ICMP probe failures are searched separately as path-MTU evidence and never converted into local drift by the primary SPL.
value: An incorrect link MTU can make large transfers stall, fragment, or underperform while small health checks continue to pass. Detecting each exact interface's deviation from its approved design value catches rebuild, automation, bonding, VLAN, tunnel, and change-window drift without paging merely because a server legitimately combines 1500-byte, jumbo, loopback, and encapsulated interfaces.
implementation: Deploy the read-only `TA_linux_mtu` collector on in-scope Linux hosts, publish an owner-approved exact `(host, interface)` MTU policy, and validate host attribution and namespace before enabling alerts. Schedule the configuration search every five minutes over 30 minutes and alert only on fresh enabled-policy mismatches. Run optional ICMP PMTU probes at lower frequency from approved sources and retain their results in a separate path-evidence search.
visualization: Use a current mismatch table with host, interface, role, observed and expected link MTU, byte delta, policy ID/owner, state, and observation age. Add separate panels for policy coverage (observed interfaces with no enabled exact policy), collector freshness, and interface MTU history. Place optional path-probe evidence in a clearly labeled panel with source interface, destination, IP family, requested packet size, small/target results, and reported next-hop MTU; do not merge it into a single configuration-mismatch count. Drill down to the raw link event, policy revision, network change, route, and same-time probe evidence.
dataModelAcceleration: No documented CIM dataset represents Linux link MTU plus exact intended configuration and policy provenance. Use the raw local source type and lookup; do not map `link_mtu` to a generic performance metric or infer intent from Network Traffic events.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row is a real difference between the latest observed value and the enabled lookup value. It can still be operationally expected or caused by bad control data.

1. **Approved change in progress** — Configuration management may apply the host before the policy export is promoted, or the reverse. Confirm the exact host, interface, intended value, UTC window, automation run, and change ticket. Update the authoritative policy in the same change; do not teach the search that all mixed values are normal.

2. **Stale or wrong policy row** — A renamed interface, repurposed NIC, changed bond/VLAN design, or host-name canonicalization change can leave an exact-match row carrying obsolete intent. Compare the row's `policy_id`, owner, role, approval date, and source design. Correct and reapprove the lookup rather than suppressing the observed configuration indefinitely.

3. **Namespace mismatch** — A forwarder running in a container or restricted network namespace can observe that namespace's `eth0`, not the host's `eth0`. The event is accurate for the collector namespace but wrong for the declared asset policy. Record namespace identity in deployment inventory and move the collector to the approved host namespace.

4. **Duplicate host attribution** — Cloned images, short-name/FQDN changes, or manually overridden `host` metadata can apply another machine's policy to an event. Reconcile forwarder GUID, host identity, interface index/MAC under restricted access, and deployment inventory before changing an MTU.

5. **Transient interface construction** — Network managers and container or virtualization tooling can briefly create a named bridge, bond, VLAN, or tunnel with a default MTU before applying its final value. The 20-minute freshness test does not require persistence. If this is common, use a deployed wrapper that requires two consecutive mismatching snapshots for that exact key; retain both raw samples.

6. **Intentional emergency deviation** — Operators may lower an MTU temporarily to restore service around a constrained path. That remains configuration drift against the normal policy even when justified. Record the exception owner, incident, exact key/value, and expiry, and restore or formally revise the policy after the incident.

**Safe suppression:** keep the catalogue SPL and policy truth unchanged. In the deployed alert wrapper only, use `linux_mtu_exceptions.csv` keyed on exact `host`, exact `interface`, and exact `observed_link_mtu`, with `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `ticket`, `owner`, and `reason`. Reject wildcards, expired rows, and exceptions lacking approval. Suppress notification actions, not collection, raw results, policy-coverage checks, or retained evidence. Path-probe failures have their own reviewed exception process because they are not configuration findings.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational Linux network configuration and path-performance monitoring; no adversary behavior is asserted)
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against Linux kernel, iproute2, iputils, IETF PMTUD, and Splunk primary sources; collector and synthetic SPL tests specified but not executed in Splunk; no runtime or SME sign-off
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement contract

Assign a Linux/platform owner, network escalation owner, Splunk content owner, and an owner for MTU policy approval. Install a supported Universal Forwarder on every in-scope Linux host. The forwarder account needs execute access to a host-provided Python 3 interpreter and the collector, permission to run the normally unprivileged `ip -j -d link show` command, and its existing outbound route to Splunk. It does not need permission to change a link, edit a route, capture packets, or run `sudo`. Optional probes require a current iputils `ping` that the forwarder account can execute under the distribution's normal datagram-socket, `ping_group_range`, setuid, or file-capability policy; do not grant broad root or `CAP_NET_ADMIN` merely for this UC.

Treat three quantities as different measurements:

1. **Observed link MTU** is the `mtu` property returned for one Linux netdevice by `ip link`. It belongs to a local interface in the collector's current network namespace.
2. **Expected link MTU** is approved configuration intent for that exact `(host, interface)` key. It comes from `linux_mtu_policy.csv`, not from another interface, a common value such as 1500 or 9000, or a probe result.
3. **Path MTU evidence** describes what one controlled source/destination/family/interface probe observed at one time. For IPv4, RFC 1191 PMTUD uses DF and ICMP Destination Unreachable/fragmentation-needed feedback. For IPv6, RFC 8201 relies on ICMPv6 Packet Too Big. ICMP feedback can be filtered, and a timeout is not a measured next-hop MTU. Path evidence therefore cannot establish which local interface or remote hop is misconfigured.

Mixed link MTUs are expected on many correct hosts. Loopback, bonds and their slaves, VLANs, bridges, veth pairs, overlay/tunnel devices, storage links, management links, and workload links can legitimately differ. This implementation alerts only when an exact enabled policy says the observed value is wrong. `index=os`, `source=linux_mtu_snapshot`, `sourcetype=linux:mtu`, app names, field names, and lookup names are deployment-owned conventions. Change them consistently if local governance requires different names.

Before rollout, identify the namespace the collector is meant to observe. `scriptExample` records `/proc/self/ns/net` as `network_namespace`; compare it with the host process namespace during acceptance. A forwarder inside a container usually sees the container's interfaces, even when its Splunk `host` field names the underlying server. That deployment must not be compared with host-interface policy.

## Step 1 — Build policy and configure collection

Package `scriptExample` as `TA_linux_mtu/bin/linux_mtu.py`, owned by the deployment account and executable. Pin the reviewed file through configuration management and retain its hash. The collector invokes executables with an argument array rather than a shell, removes inherited `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for child commands, requests locale-stable output, and uses iproute2 JSON rather than parsing human-formatted text. Physical links may have `link_type=unspecified`; do not rewrite that value to `ethernet` without a separate authoritative mapping.

Add managed scripted inputs on each Universal Forwarder:

```ini
[script://./bin/linux_mtu.py links]
disabled = 0
interval = 300
index = os
source = linux_mtu_snapshot
sourcetype = linux:mtu

[script://./bin/linux_mtu.py probes]
disabled = 1
interval = 900
index = os
source = linux_mtu_snapshot
sourcetype = linux:mtu
```

Enable the second stanza only on approved probe sources after its target list is reviewed. Splunk supports scripted inputs on universal and heavy forwarders; keep this host-local collection on the Universal Forwarder. A five-minute link interval produces 288 events per interface per day. A host with 12 visible netdevices therefore emits 3,456 small link events daily. Each enabled probe emits one event every 15 minutes, or 96 events daily. Estimate volume from representative JSON rather than claiming a universal byte rate.

Configure JSON extraction for the source type on the required parsing and search tiers:

```ini
[linux:mtu]
KV_MODE = json
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT
TRUNCATE = 0
```

Each JSON line is one event and the indexing time is the observation time. `collection_epoch` remains an independent collector clock for lag checks. Verify the winning input with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` on a test host. Execute `linux_mtu.py links` as the forwarder account and compare each emitted `interface`, `ifindex`, and `link_mtu` with the same account's `ip -j -d link show`. Do not add `sudo` if the command fails; investigate namespace, executable path, mandatory access controls, and packaging.

Create `TA_linux_mtu/lookups/linux_mtu_policy.csv` with this exact header:

```csv
host,interface,expected_link_mtu,policy_id,interface_role,policy_owner,policy_enabled
srv01.example.net,ens192,9000,DC-JUMBO-2026,application,linux-platform,true
srv01.example.net,ens224,1500,MGMT-STD-2026,management,network-operations,true
srv01.example.net,lo,65536,LINUX-LO-2026,loopback,linux-platform,true
```

Use the same canonical host value that the forwarder assigns. Every enabled row must have one literal host, one literal interface, a positive integer MTU, a durable policy ID, an operational role, and an accountable owner. Do not use wildcard hosts/interfaces, infer slave values from a bond, copy a parent MTU to a VLAN, or put temporary suppressions in policy. Review policy against the authoritative source for that host: configuration-management data, a NetworkManager connection profile, systemd-networkd unit, netplan definition, cloud-init/network metadata, orchestration inventory, or approved design record. Runtime `ip` output is observed state, not intent.

Before publishing, reject duplicate keys and malformed values:

```spl
| inputlookup linux_mtu_policy.csv
| eval expected_link_mtu=tonumber(expected_link_mtu), enabled=lower(policy_enabled)
| stats count values(expected_link_mtu) as expected_values values(policy_id) as policy_ids values(policy_owner) as owners values(enabled) as enabled_values by host interface
| where count!=1 OR mvcount(expected_values)!=1 OR mvindex(expected_values,0)<=0 OR mvfind(enabled_values,"^(true|false)$")<0
```

Configure the lookup definition for an exact string match and a maximum of one match. Preserve case consistently; Linux interface names are case-sensitive, while host normalization is a deployment decision. Restrict write permission to the policy-owner group and read permission to the search role. Treat policy changes as reviewed code or controlled data changes with an approval record.

For optional probes, create `TA_linux_mtu/local/probes.json` only on approved sources:

```json
{"probes":[{"probe_id":"srv01-to-storage-v4","target":"192.0.2.20","family":4,"interface":"ens192","expected_path_mtu":1500,"small_payload_bytes":56},{"probe_id":"srv01-to-storage-v6","target":"2001:db8::20","family":6,"interface":"ens192","expected_path_mtu":1500,"small_payload_bytes":56}]}
```

Use literal IP addresses so DNS changes do not alter the test. Obtain target-owner approval, cap each collector at the script's 16 targets, and avoid control-plane or internet destinations. The collector runs three small and three target-sized Echo Requests. `ping -s` is ICMP payload size, not link or IP packet size: this script subtracts 28 bytes for an ordinary IPv4 header plus ICMP Echo header, or 48 bytes for IPv6 plus ICMPv6, from `expected_path_mtu`. IPv4 options, extension headers, encapsulation, IPsec, tunnels, and off-path transformations invalidate that simple packet-size model and require a separately reviewed probe design. The `-I` option binds the named source interface and `-M do` selects the iputils PMTU strategy; neither identifies every hop.

## Step 2 — Create, understand, and schedule the searches

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_mtu_configuration_mismatch`. Schedule it every five minutes with a 30-minute lookback and trigger when result count is greater than zero. Its final 1,200-second age check rejects stale latest events while tolerating a few missed five-minute polls. Route by `policy_owner`, throttle notification on exact `host,interface,observed_link_mtu,expected_link_mtu` for 30 minutes, and retain every dispatch result. Do not add path-probe events to this search.

**Understanding the primary SPL:** the base search selects only `event_kind=link`. It casts MTU and collector time to numbers and rejects incomplete events. Sorting newest-first and `dedup host interface` retain one complete latest event at the exact grain used by policy, so optional fields cannot be borrowed from an older snapshot. `lookup ... OUTPUT` names only approved output fields and avoids accidental field cycles. Rows without an enabled exact policy or valid expected value do not become mismatch alerts. The inequality compares local observed configuration with explicit intent. `delta_bytes` preserves direction: negative means the configured link MTU is smaller than policy, positive means larger. Freshness filtering occurs after latest-event selection so an old interface cannot remain alertable merely because the search window is broad.

A missing policy is a data-quality issue, not evidence that the MTU is wrong. Save a separate coverage report:

```spl
index=os sourcetype=linux:mtu source=linux_mtu_snapshot event_kind=link earliest=-30m
| stats latest(_time) as observed_time latest(link_mtu) as observed_link_mtu by host interface
| lookup linux_mtu_policy.csv host interface OUTPUT expected_link_mtu policy_id policy_enabled
| where isnull(policy_id) OR lower(coalesce(policy_enabled,"false"))!="true"
| eval coverage_state=if(isnull(policy_id),"missing_policy","disabled_policy")
| table observed_time host interface observed_link_mtu coverage_state policy_id
```

Review that report during onboarding and after network-manager, container-runtime, or virtualization changes. Decide which ephemeral interfaces are explicitly out of scope in an inventory rule; do not silently treat all unlisted interfaces as MTU 1500.

Save optional probe interpretation as `linux_mtu_path_probe_evidence`:

```spl
index=os sourcetype=linux:mtu source=linux_mtu_snapshot event_kind=path_probe earliest=-30m
| eval small_probe_success=tonumber(small_probe_success), target_probe_success=tonumber(target_probe_success), reported_next_hop_mtu=tonumber(reported_next_hop_mtu)
| where small_probe_success=1 AND target_probe_success=0
| eval signal_type=if(isnotnull(reported_next_hop_mtu),"icmp_pmtu_evidence","active_probe_evidence_without_reported_mtu")
| table _time host probe_id interface target ip_family expected_path_mtu requested_packet_bytes reported_next_hop_mtu probe_outcome diagnostic signal_type
```

This supplemental search requires small-packet reachability before showing a target-size failure. When `ping` reports an MTU from local kernel or ICMP feedback, retain it as `reported_next_hop_mtu`; it is still not a complete hop attribution. Without such a value, the event says only that the sampled large Echo probes did not succeed while small ones did. ICMP rate limiting, ACLs, endpoint behavior, asymmetric paths, ECMP, transient loss, and a cached PMTU can produce the pattern. Conversely, one success proves only that the sampled packets traversed one path at that moment. Never label either result `configuration_mismatch` without link-policy evidence.

## Step 3 — Validate collection, policy, and control behavior

On at least two nonproduction hosts with different designs, compare Splunk's latest rows with `ip -j -d link show` at matching times. Include a physical or virtual workload interface, a management interface, loopback, and any bond/VLAN/tunnel relevant to policy. Confirm host canonicalization, network-namespace inode, interface name, ifindex, MTU, master, kind, and observation lag. Reconcile the intended value with the authoritative network configuration and configuration-management rendering. If the network design depends on a directly attached switch, ask the network owner to compare with the switch management interface's port-MTU view or supported CLI; the Linux value alone does not validate the peer.

Check event cadence and coverage:

```spl
index=os sourcetype=linux:mtu source=linux_mtu_snapshot earliest=-2h
| eval lag_seconds=_indextime-collection_epoch
| stats count latest(_time) as last_event avg(lag_seconds) as avg_lag max(lag_seconds) as max_lag by host event_kind
```

For links, expect approximately `visible interface count × completed polls`, allowing for deployment and scheduler timing. Run `| timechart span=5m count by host` to find gaps or duplicate inputs. Search `event_kind=collector_error` and `event_kind=collector_status` explicitly; a disabled probe file is not a failed link collector.

Execute both `controlTest` scenarios in an isolated index and test-only lookup. Keep event timestamps near execution so the final age filter accepts the positive case. Inspect the pipeline before and after the lookup. Verify that exact equality produces no row, two different interfaces with correct independent values produce no row, path events never enter the link search, a missing policy remains coverage work, and one wrong exact value returns the documented delta. This editorial rewrite specifies tests but did not run SPL in a Splunk platform runtime.

For an approved probe target, execute the collector's exact `ping` command as the forwarder account and compare exit codes and diagnostic text with the indexed event. Test a known-good expected size. If the network team has an isolated lab path where a smaller MTU can be introduced safely, record the source interface, route, target, configured bottleneck, packet sizes, ICMP policy, timestamps, and cleanup. A target-size failure with small success validates probe classification only; it does not validate the primary mismatch alert or prove the bottleneck's location. Do not impair production, disable ICMP controls, or change an MTU merely to make acceptance produce a finding.

## Step 4 — Operationalize, investigate, and preserve evidence

Build the separate panels in `visualization`. The primary mismatch KPI should count exact host/interface configuration findings only. Put policy-coverage and source-freshness KPIs beside it so a green mismatch count cannot hide missing data or missing intent. Give the path panel a title such as `Controlled PMTU probe evidence — not local configuration proof`. Restrict raw diagnostics and destination addresses to operational roles if topology is sensitive. Provide time presets for the last hour (incident), 24 hours (change review), and 30 days (drift trend).

When a configuration alert fires, the runbook should:

1. Confirm a fresh raw link event, collector namespace, and exact policy row; do not begin with a network change.
2. Run `ip -j -d link show dev <interface>` as the approved host account and compare the runtime value, master relationship, and ifindex.
3. Read the authoritative persistent configuration and the last automation/change result. Determine whether runtime drift will survive reboot or whether persistent intent itself changed.
4. Check whether a bond, bridge, VLAN, tunnel, veth, SR-IOV VF, or virtual switch owns the effective design. Validate parent/slave and encapsulation rules rather than forcing every device to one value.
5. Ask the network owner to validate the directly attached and relevant path devices when the design requires end-to-end jumbo support. A correct host value does not prove the path supports it.
6. Correlate optional path evidence, application symptoms, retransmissions, interface errors, and change timing. Keep these observations as corroboration, not replacements for configuration intent.
7. Remediate through the normal network configuration system, then require two fresh matching snapshots and, when relevant, a successful approved path test before closure.

Do not issue `ip link set`, restart networking, alter MSS clamping, clear routes, disable offloads, or relax ICMP filtering automatically from this alert. Those actions can disconnect the host or mask the actual constraint. Escalate conflicting policy to the named owner and update policy only after design approval.

Preserve the saved search and permissions, effective input stanza, source-type configuration, collector hash, exact policy revision and approval, raw before/after link events, dispatch row, source-health result, exception record, incident/change link, and control-test output according to operations retention policy. Store probe evidence separately with the exact target config and diagnostic. The `evidence` field is a deployment checklist, not a claim that these artifacts already exist.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot safely

- **No link events:** run the collector as the forwarder account; verify host Python 3, iproute2 `ip`, executable ownership/mode, namespace, and the effective scripted stanza. Search `_internal` for `ExecProcessor` messages naming `linux_mtu.py`. A collector exception emits `event_kind=collector_error` and also reaches `splunkd.log` through stderr.
- **One JSON array instead of per-interface events:** the deployed script was replaced with raw `ip -j` collection or event breaking is wrong. Restore the reviewed collector and verify `SHOULD_LINEMERGE=false`; do not build regex field extractions over human `ip link` output.
- **Fields are null:** confirm `[linux:mtu] KV_MODE=json` is deployed in the correct app context and search/parsing topology. Inspect `_raw`; do not `fillnull value=1500`, because that invents both observation and intent.
- **Observed value differs from a shell command:** align timestamps, executable, namespace inode, host identity, and interface ifindex. Interfaces can be deleted and recreated with the same name. Check for duplicate inputs and avoid comparing a container namespace with the host.
- **Every interface alerts after hostname change:** the lookup and forwarder disagree on canonical host identity, or an incorrect duplicate policy was published. Fix identity and rerun the duplicate-key audit; do not wildcard the host field.
- **Correctly mixed interfaces alert:** at least one exact policy row is wrong. The search never compares interfaces to each other. Inspect the returned expected value and policy ID instead of excluding loopback or tunnels globally.
- **No alert for an observed interface:** inspect recency, numeric `link_mtu`, exact case-sensitive interface name, host key, lookup permissions, `policy_enabled`, positive expected value, and source/index access in that order. Then check the separate policy-coverage report.
- **Transient alerts during interface creation:** correlate network-manager or orchestration timing. If accepted by design, require two consecutive mismatching snapshots in the deployed alert wrapper while keeping raw base results. Do not lengthen the stale-data allowance until old state appears current.
- **Probe events say `both_failed_inconclusive`:** verify target approval, routing, source-interface binding, namespace, address family, Echo policy, and iputils execution rights. This is reachability or collection uncertainty, not MTU evidence.
- **Small probes pass and target probes fail with no reported MTU:** retain the classification `active_probe_evidence_without_reported_mtu`. Check ICMP filtering/rate limits and path telemetry; do not fill a discovered MTU from the requested size.
- **Reported MTU conflicts with link policy:** the values answer different questions. A local interface can correctly be 9000 while a routed path is 1500, and a local interface can be wrong even when a small path works. Validate route, encapsulation, peer devices, and policy separately.
- **Probe runtime overlaps the next interval:** reduce approved targets, increase the probe interval, or distribute sources. Do not increase concurrency enough to trigger policing; Splunk schedules the next scripted invocation relative to completion.
grandmaExplanation: We compare each of a Linux computer’s network connections with its own approved size, because different connections are often supposed to be different. We also keep separate test results about how large a message traveled across a route, so the team does not blame the computer for a problem that may be somewhere along the way.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit Linux link snapshots or controlled PMTU-probe evidence for UC-1.1.60."""
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

APP_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROBE_CONFIG = APP_ROOT / "local" / "probes.json"


def emit(fields):
    base = {
        "collection_epoch": int(time.time()),
        "network_namespace": os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/net"),
    }
    base.update(fields)
    print(json.dumps(base, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True), flush=True)


def clean_env():
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("LD_LIBRARY_PATH", None)
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    return env


def run_checked(argv, timeout=20):
    return subprocess.run(
        argv,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=timeout,
        env=clean_env(),
    ).stdout


def collect_links():
    ip_cmd = shutil.which("ip")
    if not ip_cmd:
        raise RuntimeError("iproute2 ip executable not found")
    links = json.loads(run_checked([ip_cmd, "-j", "-d", "link", "show"]))
    if not isinstance(links, list):
        raise RuntimeError("ip link JSON root is not an array")
    for link in links:
        linkinfo = link.get("linkinfo") or {}
        emit({
            "event_kind": "link",
            "interface": link.get("ifname"),
            "ifindex": link.get("ifindex"),
            "link_mtu": link.get("mtu"),
            "operstate": link.get("operstate"),
            "link_type": linkinfo.get("info_kind", "unspecified"),
            "master": link.get("master", ""),
            "min_mtu": link.get("min_mtu"),
            "max_mtu": link.get("max_mtu"),
        })


def ping_once(ping_cmd, family, interface, target, payload):
    argv = [
        ping_cmd, f"-{family}", "-n", "-c", "3", "-W", "2",
        "-M", "do", "-s", str(payload), "-I", interface, target,
    ]
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            argv,
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10,
            env=clean_env(),
        )
        diagnostic = " ".join((result.stdout + " " + result.stderr).split())[:800]
        return result.returncode, diagnostic
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        diagnostic = " ".join(((exc.stdout or "") + " " + (exc.stderr or "")).split())[:800]
        return 124, "timeout " + diagnostic


def collect_probes():
    if not PROBE_CONFIG.exists():
        emit({"event_kind": "collector_status", "collector_status": "probes_disabled", "config_path": str(PROBE_CONFIG)})
        return
    ping_cmd = shutil.which("ping")
    if not ping_cmd:
        raise RuntimeError("iputils ping executable not found")
    config = json.loads(PROBE_CONFIG.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    probes = config.get("probes", [])
    if not isinstance(probes, list) or len(probes) > 16:
        raise RuntimeError("probes must be an array with at most 16 entries")
    for probe in probes:
        probe_id = str(probe["probe_id"])
        target = str(probe["target"])
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(target)
        family = int(probe.get("family", address.version))
        if family not in (4, 6) or address.version != family:
            raise ValueError(f"family mismatch for {probe_id}")
        interface = str(probe["interface"])
        expected_path_mtu = int(probe["expected_path_mtu"])
        header_bytes = 28 if family == 4 else 48
        target_payload = expected_path_mtu - header_bytes
        small_payload = int(probe.get("small_payload_bytes", 56))
        if not interface or target_payload <= small_payload or expected_path_mtu > 65535:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid interface or size for {probe_id}")
        small_rc, small_diag = ping_once(ping_cmd, family, interface, target, small_payload)
        target_rc, target_diag = ping_once(ping_cmd, family, interface, target, target_payload)
        mtu_matches = re.findall(r"(?i)mtu[ =](\d+)", target_diag)
        reported_mtu = int(mtu_matches[-1]) if mtu_matches else None
        if small_rc == 0 and target_rc == 0:
            outcome = "target_passed"
        elif small_rc == 0:
            outcome = "target_failed_small_passed"
        elif target_rc == 0:
            outcome = "target_passed_small_failed"
        else:
            outcome = "both_failed_inconclusive"
        emit({
            "event_kind": "path_probe",
            "probe_id": probe_id,
            "target": target,
            "ip_family": family,
            "interface": interface,
            "expected_path_mtu": expected_path_mtu,
            "target_payload_bytes": target_payload,
            "requested_packet_bytes": target_payload + header_bytes,
            "small_payload_bytes": small_payload,
            "small_probe_success": int(small_rc == 0),
            "target_probe_success": int(target_rc == 0),
            "small_result_code": small_rc,
            "target_result_code": target_rc,
            "probe_outcome": outcome,
            "reported_next_hop_mtu": reported_mtu,
            "diagnostic": ("small: " + small_diag + " | target: " + target_diag)[:1500],
        })


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2 or sys.argv[1] not in {"links", "probes"}:
        raise SystemExit("usage: linux_mtu.py links|probes")
    if sys.argv[1] == "links":
        collect_links()
    else:
        collect_probes()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as exc:
        emit({"event_kind": "collector_error", "error_type": type(exc).__name__, "error": str(exc)[:500]})
        raise
